stories.title: You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
stories.simple_summary: Google is letting people remove the visible sparkly watermark that appears on images and videos created by its AI tools. The watermark will still exist invisibly in the background to track that it's AI-made.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google's AI tools to create images or videos, you now have the choice to hide the watermark — but honestly, this mostly affects people making content for social media or business use.

stories.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
stories.simple_summary: Google's AI image and video tools will let users hide the visible watermark while keeping a hidden watermark that only Google's systems can detect.
stories.why_it_matters: Same as above — this is mainly for people actively creating content with Google's AI, not something most small business owners need to think about.

stories.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for everyone’?
stories.simple_summary: Meta released an AI tool called Glimmer that anyone can download and use on their own computer, and Mark Zuckerberg said AI should be available to everyone rather than locked away by big companies.
stories.why_it_matters: If you want to experiment with AI tools, Meta is making one easier to access than before — but this is mostly important for tech enthusiasts and doesn't change much for everyday use.

stories.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
stories.simple_summary: A company called Kog thinks there's a better way to run AI on the special computer chips that power AI systems, and that those chips aren't as bad at certain jobs as people thought.
stories.why_it_matters: This is purely a technical matter for engineers and data centers — nothing relevant to your business or daily life.

stories.title: Hyperscalers might regret embracing natural gas if new forecast proves correct
stories.simple_summary: If natural gas prices jump sharply in the coming years, the huge computer warehouses that power AI services could face very expensive electricity bills.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually make AI services more expensive for companies that use them, but that's still uncertain and not something to worry about right now.

stories.title: Meta’s ‘open’ AI, and a $250M deal gone very wrong
stories.simple_summary: Meta released a free AI tool people can use themselves while keeping a more powerful AI tool locked to its own service, alongside Mark Zuckerberg's statement that AI should belong to everyone.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a philosophical and business question for tech investors — the practical impact on ordinary people is very limited.

stories.title: Apple trained its own AI model for China with help from Alibaba
stories.simple_summary: Apple created a custom AI system specifically for the Chinese market by working with a Chinese company called Alibaba.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly news about big companies' international business deals — it doesn't affect you unless you're very invested in Apple's operations in China.

stories.title: Microsoft’s Clippy-like Mico character is no longer the face of Copilot
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is moving away from showing a friendly yellow cartoon character when you talk to its Copilot AI assistant.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just a small change to how the tool looks — nothing that changes how it actually works or affects whether you use it.

stories.title: Writer introduces new AI model and upgraded harness to contain token costs
stories.simple_summary: A company called Writer released a new AI model designed to be cheaper and faster to run than previous versions.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to companies that pay for AI services — it could eventually lead to cheaper AI tools, but nothing immediate for most people.

stories.title: Databricks wanted to raise $1B, investors wanted $15B. It settled on $5B at a $190B valuation.
stories.simple_summary: A company called Databricks that builds AI tools wanted to raise a certain amount of money from investors but ended up getting more offers than expected, so it raised even more at a higher value.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investor news showing that AI companies are attracting lots of money — nothing that directly affects you.

stories.title: OpenAI is losing its second executive this week
stories.simple_summary: Two important executives are leaving OpenAI to take other jobs, and new people are replacing them.
stories.why_it_matters: Personnel changes at big tech companies don't usually affect how their products work or your ability to use them.

stories.title: OpenAI introduces ‘Ultrafast,’ a new mode that makes GPT-5.6 Sol work at 14x the speed
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is offering a faster version of its most powerful AI model that works 14 times quicker than the regular version.
stories.why_it_matters: If you pay to use OpenAI's AI, a faster version could be helpful — but this is mainly targeting large businesses, not individual small business owners yet.
